author: blueiridium.
content:
Hi, I’ve continued looking into slashing edge cases. I found one remaining thing I’m unsure about. It is a **Gloas-specific way to fragment attester-slashing proofs**. [EIP-7732](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7732) uses a signed 0/1 value to signal payload status. For an eligible past-block vote, an equivocating cohort can split across those values while voting for the same block root. Because a slashing proof pairs two specific signed attestation messages, slashing the cohort may then require multiple proofs. Blocks can include only one attester slashing each.

There’s also a pre-Gloas route to the same proof-count effect: split votes across different block roots. That requires multiple eligible roots and votes that satisfy the ordinary attestation rules. The Gloas status value adds a way to split votes on the *same* root, subject to its payload conditions.

I can reproduce the fragmentation, but **I haven’t demonstrated an impact**: no unslashed withdrawal, safety failure, or economic loss. Can anyone see a concrete consequence, including with [EIP-8061’s](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8061) proposed increase in exit churn, or is this an understood by the team and not expected to produce any negative outcomes?
